# Template: line_chart
A line chart from data: one or more series over a numeric or categorical x, each line ending in its own name, drawn as ink so it animates as geometry. `values` may be one list (static) or a list of lists — STAGES of the same chart — and the numeric `stage` param picks which one is shown; a fractional stage interpolates, so `animate: {stage: 1}` plays the change, and a series given prefix by prefix draws itself in from its last point. Feed it typed numbers, or a code element's variables via "{id.var}" tokens (name the series by hand so the line_k beats exist before the script has run). `slope: true` switches to a slope chart — two labelled columns and one straight connector per series, named and valued at BOTH ends — for before/after, two time points, or Simpson's paradox. A line race adds three more params: `ticker` writes the year large and dim in the plot's corner; `x_window: n` slides a rolling window over the last n x positions instead of showing the whole span; and `label_top: n`, which is the EXCEPTION — normally every line keeps its name for the whole race, and two names that come close are dimmed where they cross rather than one of them being dropped. All three are ignored in slope mode, which always shows exactly two columns with every series already named and valued at both ends. Choose this scene for ANY request for a line chart, a trend over time, a curve computed from data, two scenarios compared over time, a slope chart, a line race, or "show how this develops". GUESSABLE: an ask with `on: line_1` and `from: <x>` lets the viewer draw the rest of the line before the true line is drawn. Up to 200 stages, but each series is its OWN harvest token, capped at 5000 numbers independently of the others — a single line fits 200 stages × 25 points, 200 × 40 does not. The 12-series cap is a separate ceiling; it never multiplies against a series' own harvest cap the way bar_chart's single shared `values` token does.

Only the N highest lines at the current stage carry their name at the end; the rest stay drawn but unlabelled. Because the ranking is re-read at every stage, a line that slips out of the top N LOSES its name and gets it back when it climbs — names blinking on and off as the race runs, which is almost never what a race wants. A race would rather let two names sit close for a moment (they are dimmed where they cross, so the overlap reads as ink over ink) than take a name away. Reach for it only when the field is genuinely too crowded to name at once, or when the disappearing name IS the point the narration makes — never to avoid a collision, which is handled by the dimming. Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the x and y axes with their captions and end values (slope: true — axes__col0/axes__col1 name the two columns instead of an x scale)
- line_1: the first series: its polyline, optional dots, and its name at the end (line_2, … likewise — every series keeps its name unless the exceptional label_top excludes it); with slope: true it is instead the straight connector between two columns, its name and value drawn at both ends
- ticker: the large dimmed stage caption, when set
- note: the refusal note, drawn only when slope: true and a series does not have exactly two values
- title: figure title, when set
